findings.evidence: On the exact r1 candidate, a valid PRD golden was changed from author_id='author-prd', reviewer_id='reviewer-prd' to author_id='REVIEWER-PRD', reviewer_id='reviewer-prd', with the artifact digest recomputed. ArtifactValidator.validate returned PASS with no failures. records.py compares raw strings case-sensitively and accepts whitespace/case variants, contrary to Spec sections 4.1 and 6.3 requiring normalized canonical actors to differ.
findings.required_fix: Define and enforce one canonical ActorRef normalization/validation rule before author/reviewer comparison, including surrounding-whitespace rejection and case-insensitive identity comparison. Bind matrix REVIEW tests for case and whitespace variants across all ten artifact types.
findings.summary: Canonical actor independence can be bypassed with case variants.

findings.evidence: Three production-API counterexamples reproduced on r1: (1) replacing a golden target with caller-invented target_id='attacker-target' and a syntactically valid digest, while updating its decision trace, returned PASS because validate has no expected-target registry; (2) adding a second known typed input without a dependency trace returned PASS; (3) adding a second correctly oriented known requirement trace returned FAIL with traces/status because trace_types is compared as an exact three-element list rather than allowing multiple closed traces of each required type. Thus caller-derived target nodes are trusted, missing edges are accepted, and real multi-requirement artifacts are rejected.
findings.required_fix: Require exact externally supplied current target bindings, including target ID/digest/task, and validate trace closure per occurrence: every input must have the required input-to-artifact dependency trace, every declared target its artifact-to-target decision trace, and all applicable requirements their requirement-to-artifact traces. Permit multiple distinct traces of an allowed type while rejecting duplicate edges. Add positive multi-input/multi-target/multi-requirement cases and negative omitted-edge and target-forgery cases to each relevant matrix cell.
findings.summary: Typed target authority and multi-reference trace closure are not enforced.

findings.evidence: A 2,097,153-byte physical body was accepted although the bound ResourceProfile raw_document_bytes limit is 1,048,576. Comparing otherwise equivalent one-byte and 2,097,153-byte manifests produced identical 1,521-event operation traces and identical final balances, proving raw_digest over the physical body and selector extraction work are outside WorkContext accounting. This permits input-size-dependent work beyond both hard limits and deterministic budget traces.
findings.required_fix: Before hashing or slicing physical bytes, enforce raw_document_bytes and applicable selector/result/temp limits, and charge every physical/extracted digest input byte in normative operation-path order before work. Add exact small/limit/over-one cases plus per-occurrence amount-minus-one atomic rejection and full trace/balance comparisons.
findings.summary: LogicalBodyManifest hashes unbounded physical bytes without hard-limit or work charging.

findings.evidence: A revision-2 Impact record superseding an accepted_for_next_node revision was changed to status='candidate', given body-digest progress and correctly rebound records, and ArtifactValidator.validate returned PASS; ArtifactLifecycle.require_transition('accepted_for_next_node','candidate') rejects the same transition. Separately, public constructors accepted ArtifactValidationRecord('forged',None,'PASS',(),()) and an arbitrary valid-looking ArtifactLifecycleEvent. The lifecycle event contains no body_digest and is not derived from an attested ArtifactRecord or charged self-digest.
findings.required_fix: Integrate previous-to-current closed-state validation into revision loading, and make validation/lifecycle evidence factory-only products of exact validated records. Bind immutable lifecycle events to artifact ID, artifact digest, body digest, revision, prior/current status, and charged event identity. Add every forbidden revision transition and direct-constructor/forgery regression.
findings.summary: Revision validation is disconnected from the closed lifecycle and audit evidence is forgeable.

findings.evidence: Two valid manifests with identical artifact selectors and extracted digests but different unselected separator bytes, manifest_id, and mode had different manifest digests; LogicalBodyManifest.invalidated_by returned an empty tuple. Existing ArtifactRecords bind manifest_id and manifest_digest, so those same records cease to validate against the new manifest while the invalidation engine reports no change. The current comparison ignores manifest_id, mode, physical_body_digest, and manifest_digest.
findings.required_fix: Define comparable manifest lineage and make invalidation cover every field that changes ArtifactRecord validity. Either reject unrelated manifest IDs/modes as incomparable or deterministically invalidate the exact affected records when physical/manifest metadata changes. Add gap-byte, manifest-ID, mode, physical-digest, selector, dependency, and shared-section cases that cross-check invalidation output against actual record revalidation.
findings.summary: Manifest invalidation can report no affected artifact after a binding-significant manifest change.

findings.evidence: Fresh evidence rebuild/replay and scripts/run_wp04a_gate.py both reported PASS, including 280 full tests and all declared 100 IDs, while the five production counterexamples above remain reproducible. Matrix INPUTS uses one input and no authoritative target map, REVIEW checks only literal equality, STATUS tests a detached state-table call rather than revision integration, INVALIDATE changes only one first semantic field and asserts self-invalidation, and no WP-04A budget-trace boundary suite exists. test_exact_case_id_product_is_complete reconstructs the same in-code product rather than proving required submutations execute.
findings.required_fix: Replace surface case-ID coverage with gate-bound mutation manifests listing every required subcase and asserting each executes against production APIs. Include canonical identity variants, multi-ref closure, authoritative target swaps, every lifecycle/revision transition, direct forgery, manifest metadata changes, and exact hard-limit/work-budget traces; fail coverage when any declared mutation lacks a failing or positive fixture.
findings.summary: The exact 10×10 gate proves test IDs exist but does not mechanically cover the normative mutation product.
